blocks.text: 1. Modular RAG
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447720038-199996244.png

Advanced RAG named the general strategy of adding correction stages and identified itself as a family of specific techniques. Modular RAG, treating each pipeline stage as a swappable, independent module, is the architectural pattern that makes assembling those techniques practical.
Each stage exposes a fixed interface so it can be replaced without touching the rest.
2. From A Fixed Chain To Swappable Modules
Naive RAG, covered in Naive RAG, hardcodes one fixed sequence of stages.
Modular RAG defines each stage as an interchangeable module instead.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Architecture","How stages are defined"],"rows":[["Naive RAG","One fixed, hardcoded sequence of stages"],["Modular RAG","Independent modules with a fixed interface"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Common Modules In A RAG Pipeline

blocks.alt: Common Modules In A RAG Pipeline
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447720039-238948585.png
A query module, a retrieval module, a re-rank module, and a generation module each handle one job.
Each module can be swapped for a different implementation independently.
4. Routing Between Modules
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447720040-535237375.png
A routing layer decides which specific module implementation to invoke for a given query.
Different query types can flow through a different combination of modules.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A routing layer that sends a factual lookup query through a lightweight retrieval module, while a complex comparison query flows through a heavier module combination, is a common modular RAG pattern.

blocks.text: 5. Loops And Conditional Flows
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447720040-33036081.png
Unlike naive RAG's strictly linear flow, covered in Naive RAG, modular RAG allows a module to be revisited.
A retrieval module can be called again if a later module flags the result as insufficient.
6. Testing Modules In Isolation
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447720041-577925333.png
Because each module exposes a fixed interface, it can be tested on its own.
There is no need to run the entire end to end pipeline just to validate one change.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Testing approach","What it requires"],"rows":[["Fixed monolithic pipeline","Running the full end to end pipeline to validate any change"],["Modular pipeline","Testing the one changed module in isolation"]]}

blocks.text: 7. Modular RAG Enables The Other Patterns

blocks.alt: Modular RAG Enables The Other Patterns
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447720041-376675962.png
Corrective RAG, self-RAG, and adaptive RAG, covered next in this module, are each implemented as a specific module combination.
Modularity is what makes assembling those specific patterns practical.
8. Added Architectural Complexity
As with each added step costing latency, covered in Advanced RAG, defining clean module boundaries and a routing layer takes real upfront engineering effort.
That effort becomes worthwhile once the pipeline needs to support several different query types.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Building a routing layer and clean module interfaces adds real upfront engineering work, a cost that pays off once the pipeline actually needs to support several distinct query types.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Modular RAG Earns Its Added Engineering Effort

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Modular RAG Earns Its Added Engineering Effort
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447720042-816668765.png
A system serving several distinct query types benefits from swappable modules.
A single, fixed query pattern, by contrast, rarely needs the added modularity.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates a minimal modular pipeline with swappable retrieval modules chosen by a router.

code.content:
def simple_retrieval_module(query, chunks):
    # common modules in a RAG pipeline
    return chunks[:2]

def multi_hop_retrieval_module(query, chunks):
    # common modules in a RAG pipeline
    return chunks

def router(query):
    # routing between modules
    if " and " in query.lower():
        return multi_hop_retrieval_module
    return simple_retrieval_module

def generation_module(chunks, query):
    context = "\n".join(f"- {c}" for c in chunks)
    return f"Context:\n{context}\n\nQuestion: {query}\nAnswer:"

chunks = [
    "The Falcon plan costs twenty dollars per month.",
    "The Eagle plan costs thirty five dollars per month.",
    "Refunds are processed within five business days.",
]

for query in ["What does the Falcon plan cost?", "Compare the Falcon plan and the Eagle plan"]:
    retrieval_module = router(query)
    retrieved = retrieval_module(query, chunks)
    prompt = generation_module(retrieved, query)
    print(f"Query: {query}")
    print(f"Routed to: {retrieval_module.__name__}")
    print(f"Retrieved: {retrieved}\n")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the router selecting a different retrieval module depending on whether the query needs one fact or several, the core benefit of a modular design.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Building tightly coupled stages that cannot actually be swapped independently despite being called modules.
Adding a routing layer without a real need for more than one module implementation per stage.
Skipping isolated tests for individual modules and only testing the full pipeline end to end.
Over-engineering a modular architecture for a system with only one fixed query pattern.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Modular RAG treats each pipeline stage as a swappable, independent module with a fixed interface.
Naive RAG hardcodes one fixed sequence; modular RAG defines interchangeable modules instead.
Query, retrieval, re-rank, and generation modules each handle one job independently.
A routing layer decides which module implementation to invoke for a given query.
Modular RAG allows loops, letting a module be revisited when a later step flags insufficiency.
A fixed module interface allows testing each module in isolation, not just the full pipeline.
Corrective RAG, self-RAG, and adaptive RAG are each implemented as specific module combinations.
Clean module boundaries take real upfront engineering effort, worthwhile for varied query types.
Next up: Corrective RAG (CRAG), covering a specific module that grades and corrects poor retrieval.
